title: Writes are gated; refusals are shown
lede: Read-only by default. A write needs the connection switch; a refusal from the console is shown honestly. Simulated in Mock.

nodes.label: Your browser
sub: Writes are off unless you switch them on for the connection.

nodes.label: This app (server)
sub: allowWrites per connection; DELETE and PATCH always need it.

nodes.label: Audit log
sub: Every call: ok, refused or error. Secret redacted.

nodes.label: Privilege console API
sub: 401 / 403 on a wrong or scoped-out key is passed through.

steps.title: A write is attempted
steps.what: A POST, PUT, DELETE or PATCH on a connection with writes off.

steps.title: The gate checks allowWrites
steps.what: POST and PUT run with writes off only if the body is empty-by-spec; DELETE and PATCH always need the switch.

steps.title: Blocked, honestly
steps.what: The gate answers 403 writes_disabled and records the block. The page says how to turn writes on.

steps.title: Or the call goes out
steps.what: With writes on, the call goes to the console with the key headers.

steps.title: A refusal is passed through
steps.what: The console's own 401/403 (wrong key, scope too small, admin collection not allowed) is shown as-is.

steps.title: Everything is audited
steps.what: ok, refused, blocked or error: the audit log keeps it, redacted.
